guide: Open Start and type your business name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the owner draw, the set-aside share, the cash floor, the months of cover, the red and amber days for renewals and the training hours you want.
A doula is a non-medical support person who helps a client before, during or after a birth. A solo doula keeps one row per person and no backup doula.
Write each month in Profit and Loss and Cash by Month. The revenue, profit, margin, cost per birth and months of cover fill in by themselves.
Keep Expenses up to date and set a monthly Budget for each category. Budget vs Actual then shows every category and month against the budget and last year.

Check Contracts, Instalments and Clients. They give the cash expected from balances and payment plans and the unearned balance (cash received for work not yet done). An hour pack is a set number of postpartum hours bought together.
Read Cash Forecast for the next 12 months: expected cash in, costs, owner pay, set-aside, the lowest month and the best and worst cases.
Use Owner Pay Plan and Tax Set-aside to decide your draw. The set-aside share is an example: confirm it with your adviser.
Record every renewal in Renewals and every training in Training. Renewal Calendar shows the next ones with red and amber status and Training Hours by Holder shows the hours of each doula.
Open Own History Compare, Year in Review and Year Plan at month end and year end to compare with your own history and set next year's births a month.
Use the 18 tools to answer the weekly money questions: cash, draw, set-aside, break-even, time off and the accountant pack.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Money Dashboard and the charts every month. A solo doula uses the same sheets as a one-person money sheet with one doula and no backup rota.

listing.title: Doula Business Money Excel Template: Profit and Loss, Cash Flow Forecast, Owner Pay, Tax Set-Aside, Renewals Tracker, Budget vs Actual
listing.headline: Know your cash, your pay and your renewal dates before they surprise you
listing.description:
Run the money side of your doula business in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-doula who also takes clients, contracted doulas, backup doulas and a part-time admin, and just as useful for a solo doula who wants a one-person money sheet. Profit and Loss and Cash by Month turn your monthly figures into revenue, profit, margin, cost per birth, doula pay share and months of cover. Expenses, Budget and Budget vs Actual rank every category against the monthly budget and the same month last year. Contracts show the cash received and the unearned balance (cash received for work not yet done) for every package.

Cash Forecast builds an uneven-month forecast for the next 12 months from due dates, balances and payment plans, with the lowest month, the months of cover and a best and worst case. Owner Pay Plan and Tax Set-aside show whether you can pay yourself this month and what to move aside (confirm the share with your adviser). Renewals, Training, Renewal Calendar and Training Hours by Holder give red and amber warnings, the cost of the year and the training hours of each doula.

18 tools answer the weekly questions: training and renewal dates, expense tracker, cash forecast, owner pay, profit ratios, compare with your own history, year-end summary and next-year plan, cash runway, budget ranking, break-even births a month, draw scenario, set-aside check, free cash, renewal costs, time-off test, cash cushion, fixed costs and an accountant pack check. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the owner-doula, doulas, backup doulas, the admin, the accountant and the insurer.

This is part eight of the Doula Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Clients appear by name only and no medical detail is recorded. It helps you keep track of hours, dates, money and capacity and does not promise any result. Check your local rules for records, insurance and tax.
